candidate_relations.reason: The reference diagnosis centers on organized thrombus on the native bicuspid aortic valve combined with ascending aortic aneurysm. C001 describes the structural valve disease and aneurysm but entirely omits the thrombus, which is the key diagnostic element confirmed histopathologically and intraoperatively.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Captures BAV with AR and ascending aortic aneurysm but omits the organized thrombus formation, which is the defining pathological finding

candidate_relations.reason: The intraoperative and histopathological findings confirm an organized thrombus on the left coronary cusp of the aortic valve covering the coronary ostium, not occlusion of the coronary artery itself. C002 misattributes the anatomical site and implies coronary artery pathology rather than valvular thrombus.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Describes thrombotic occlusion of the left coronary artery rather than thrombus on the aortic valve cusp; also omits ascending aortic aneurysm

candidate_relations.reason: C003 captures the thrombus component and its location, which is the central pathological finding, but does not specify the bicuspid aortic valve as the native valve substrate nor the concurrent ascending aortic aneurysm, both of which are required components of the reference diagnosis.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Correctly identifies aortic valve thrombosis at the left coronary cusp but omits the bicuspid valve substrate and the ascending aortic aneurysm

candidate_relations.reason: C004 addresses only the structural valve disease component. It misses the organized thrombus (the defining pathological finding) and the ascending aortic aneurysm, making it an incomplete representation of the reference diagnosis.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Identifies BAV with AR but omits both the organized thrombus and the ascending aortic aneurysm

candidate_relations.reason: C005 addresses only the aneurysm component with specific dimensions. It omits the organized thrombus on the native bicuspid aortic valve, which is the primary diagnostic finding confirmed by intraoperative and histopathological examination.
